title: Long BTC — Post-Stop-Trigger Re-entry; $60K–$62K Base + DXY Gate Required
entry: CONDITIONAL — do NOT enter until both conditions are simultaneously met: (1) BTC closes in the $60,000–$62,000 zone on two consecutive UTC daily sessions, establishing a stabilization base after the June 19 stop-trigger event; AND (2) DXY closes below 99.00 on the same or immediately prior session, confirming the BUY regime upgrade is in effect. At current price ($62,522 live June 19, 11:06 UTC), the stop clock is completing and BTC is NOT yet at the re-entry zone. Do NOT catch the falling knife between $62,500 and $60,000. If BTC stabilizes at $60,000–$62,000 AND DXY clears the gate: enter 60% initial position; reserve 40% to add on any first-week dip to $59,500–$61,000 that holds above $58,000. Do NOT enter if BTC breaks below $58,000 on two consecutive sessions — that signals capitulation, not stabilization.
stop_loss: $56,000 daily close — below the BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF institutional demand zone and the YTD 2026 consolidation support; two consecutive closes below $58,000 would be an early warning signal but not the formal stop; $56,000 represents an 8% loss from the $61,000 entry midpoint and implies BTC has broken through every established support level in the current range, requiring a full re-assessment of the risk framework before any further crypto exposure
targets: $68,000 — reclaim of the pre-stop level; DXY confirmed below 99.00; June 19 stop event absorbed with no cascading liquidation; institutional ETF accumulation visible in volume profiles; +11.5% from $61K entry midpoint
$75,000 — full BUY regime upgrade confirmed: SPX above 7,460, VIX below 18, DXY below 99.00 all in place simultaneously; risk-on posture accelerates institutional inflows into BTC ETFs; +22.9%

$82,000 — blue sky: May PCE June 25 prints below 3.5% YoY, triggering a Warsh pivot signal (nine dots begin to reprice toward neutral); 30Y falls below 4.70%; BTC as a high-duration asset disproportionately benefits from rate re-pricing; +34.4%
risk_reward: 1:4.2 to third target (from $61K midpoint, stop $56K = risk $5K; T3 $82K = gain $21K)
catalyst: The June 19 UTC midnight close will almost certainly confirm Day 2 of the two-day systematic stop clock, triggering the exit of the BTC long position at the $63,500 threshold. BTC at $62,522.82 (live, Crypto.com MCP, 11:06 UTC June 19) is making lower lows, having rejected the 24h high of $64,450 in the early Asian session. This creates the setup: once the stop event is confirmed and sellers are exhausted, the $60,000–$62,000 zone represents the next institutional demand base, anchored by the BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF's estimated $4–6B accumulation range. The DXY gate precondition ensures this re-entry only activates when the macro regime has shifted in BTC's favor.
thesis:
The June 19 stop trigger is mechanically driven by the Warsh hawkish FOMC outcome — nine hike dots, 3.8% 2026 median, no forward guidance. BTC is a high-duration asset: it has zero coupon-equivalent cashflow and its valuation is entirely a function of the discount rate applied to speculative future adoption scenarios. When Warsh projects nine rate hikes into a 3.8% median rate path, the discount rate applied to BTC's future cash-flow-equivalent appreciation rises by exactly the same mechanism that compresses SPCX or high-multiple growth equities. The Iran deal disinflation thesis — that lower oil prices reduce Fed hawkishness, reducing the discount rate, benefiting BTC — was overwhelmed by the explicit rate path signal. DXY at 100.15 after oil crashed 5% is the proof: the market is pricing Warsh's dots, not commodity disinflation.

The re-entry case at $60,000–$62,000 rests on two conditions that are explicitly interdependent. First, BTC must stabilize at this level for two sessions — establishing that the stop event did not trigger cascading liquidation (leveraged long liquidations feeding into further selling). A two-session stabilization with decreasing volume on down days confirms the sellers are exhausted and the level represents genuine buy-side support. Second, DXY must close below 99.00, confirming that the macro constraint blocking the BUY upgrade has cleared. In the scenario where DXY breaks below 99.00, the Iran deal disinflation has finally overwhelmed the Warsh rate premium in the FX market — which is precisely the catalyst that would reduce BTC's discount rate and restore the risk-on bid.

The $60,000–$62,000 zone has structural significance beyond the current setup. This level corresponds to the BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF's estimated accumulation range, which has been confirmed as a support floor across three prior tests in 2026. Institutional ETF inflows are the new marginal buyer in Bitcoin — replacing the retail speculation that dominated in 2020–2021. The ETF buyer base is mechanically less volatile: they buy on dollar-cost-average schedules rather than on momentum, which means support levels are stickier than historical BTC support zones. If the ETF bid is present at $60,000–$62,000 (confirmed by volume profile), the re-entry has a structurally different risk profile than a retail momentum chase.

This is explicitly a low-conviction, small-size (2%) conditional opportunity. Do NOT enter BTC before the DXY gate clears, regardless of how compelling the $61,000 level looks. The DXY gate is the regime condition: if DXY is above 99.00, the Warsh hawkish premium is still intact, BTC faces continued duration headwinds, and the $56,000 stop might not even hold. The 2% position size is sized for a conditional trade that activates only in the BUY upgrade regime, where risk appetite is high and the macro setup supports it. The $82,000 blue-sky scenario (PCE below 3.5% on June 25) is a ~10–15% probability event but would be an extremely powerful BTC catalyst: repricing nine Warsh hike dots toward neutral would benefit high-duration assets disproportionately and could take BTC to $80,000+ in a single week.
bull_case: BTC closes at $61,500 on June 19 UTC midnight, confirming the two-day stop event cleanly without cascading liquidation. Monday June 22 DXY opens below 100.00 and closes at 98.80 — Gate 3 cleared, BUY upgrade fires. BTC finds the $60,000 re-entry zone on Tuesday June 23 (DXY confirmation day + mild risk-asset profit-taking). Position entered at $60,500. MU earnings June 24 and NVDA Annual Meeting deliver constructive read-throughs for the AI/crypto complex. May PCE June 25 prints 3.8% (at or slightly below Wells Fargo estimate), not disinflationary but below 4.0% which avoids the STEP_ASIDE scenario. BTC recovers to $68,000 by July 4 on the full risk-on BUY posture.
bear_case: BTC stop confirms June 19 but immediately cascades: leveraged long liquidations accelerate the move to $58,000–$59,000 within 48 hours, breaking below the BlackRock ETF demand zone and triggering a second wave of selling. DXY holds above 100.00 on Monday June 22 as Warsh dominates. May PCE June 25 prints 4.3% — 30Y breaches 5.00%, VIX spikes above 20, STEP_ASIDE scenario. BTC falls to $52,000–$55,000 zone. The conditional re-entry at $60,000–$62,000 is never activated because the DXY gate never clears. In this scenario, the position is not entered (correctly, per the framework) and capital is preserved.
invalidation: $56,000 daily close (formal stop if position entered); OR DXY fails to close below 99.00 within 3 weeks of the June 19 stop event, making this re-entry thesis stale (expires July 8 regardless); OR BTC breaks below $58,000 on two consecutive sessions before stabilizing (capitulation signal — do not enter); OR May PCE June 25 prints above 4.0% AND VIX spikes above 20 (STEP_ASIDE scenario — no crypto exposure appropriate); OR BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF reports three consecutive weeks of net outflows (institutional demand floor has cracked)
